title: Podium Of Three
description:
## Task

A contest records each entrant as a name and a score. Rank entrants from the highest score to the lowest; when two scores tie, the name that comes first alphabetically ranks higher. Return the names of the top three entrants (or all of them if there are fewer than three).

## Input

- `names` — a list of distinct, non-empty lowercase strings, one per entrant. It may be empty.
- `scores` — a list of integers, the same length as `names`; `scores[i]` belongs to `names[i]`.

## Output

A list of up to three names, best first.

## Example

```python
podium_names(['ana', 'bo', 'cy', 'di'], [70, 90, 70, 50])  # returns ['bo', 'ana', 'cy']
podium_names(['zed'], [5])  # returns ['zed']
```

## Constraints

- 0 ≤ length of `names` ≤ 10^4
- -10^6 ≤ each score ≤ 10^6
signature: def podium_names(names: list[str], scores: list[int]) -> list[str]
